maria: Heads-up: after the 03:00 deploy we saw a ~12% tail latency regression on hosted inference. Traces point to host-side costs (tokenization + request parse) and a lot more small writev syscalls from the gateway.

aj: ugh. any flamegraphs or pprof?

maria: pasted short flame snippet from pprof:
```
--- host_total ---
parse_request 38.2%
 tokenization 22.1%
 serialize_chunks 9.8%
 grpc_writev 12.7%
 scheduling_wait 5.4%
 others 11.8%
```
Looks like parse_request + tokenization are the big ones, but there's a churn of small `writev` calls during streaming.

ken: could be fragmentation from our chunking heuristics. If clients send lots of small pieces we do per-chunk proto marshalling + write.

sophia: @maria can you share example payloads? I want to reproduce with wrk/httperf.

maria: quick sample (sanitized):
```json
{"input": "<long prompt>... split into ~16 pieces by client framing"}
```
We get 8-20 writev calls per token burst in some sessions.

aj: that explains the syscall overhead. We should try coalescing at the gateway: aggregate up to 32k or timeout 3ms before write.

ken: agree. Also kernel selection: if runtime picks AVX512 kernels for short sequences it can be worse. Need to force small-seq optimized kernels for these request shapes.

maria: evidence for kernel mischoice: compare two runs with same model on same hw: when seq_len < 64 we see worse cycles/sec and more L1 cache misses with the current runtime kernel policy.

infra-bot: deploy-log: canary rollout started for service=gw-hosting at 03:00. 5% -> 50% -> 100% completed.

aj: propose short plan: 1) short-term gateway coalesce patch, 2) add micro-batching at parsing layer (batch up to N concurrent parse jobs before tokenize), 3) runtime kernel policy tweak for seq<64 -> small-kernel.

sophia: for KV cache: any correlation with cache evictions? If many small requests bypass prefix cache we might thrash dentry & cause extra copies.

maria: yes, KV metrics show a spike in KV write events and 2x higher eviction rate around the same window. Might be related to our experimental per-request prefix invalidation logic.

ken: that invalidation was supposed to be safe but I can revert quickly. It's a config flag: `kv.prefix_invalidate=true` -> set false to test.

aj: also instrument socket buffer sizes: if send buffers are tiny we end up with multiple system calls. `SO_SNDBUF` check + set to 256k for gw process.

maria: I've queued an infra runbook checklist:
- revert kv.prefix_invalidate flag -> roll out to canary (maria)
- add write coalesce (aj) with 3ms flush timer -> canary
- bump SO_SNDBUF in container runtime -> ops
- add kernel-policy override for seq<64 -> runtime team (ken)
- capture microprofiles + tcpdump for 5 min after each step

ken: I'll try a local perf run with `perf record -F 99 -g --` and compare kernel stacks. Might also try `numactl --interleave=all` to rule out numa skew.

sophia: for reproducer, I'll craft a client that streams many small frames (16-64B) at high QPS and include KV-prefetch header to exercise cache. If anyone wants to pair DM me.

aj: one more observation: grpc writev code path adds a 7-10us mutex in trace samples per call when we use the per-chunk buffer pool. We should try a lock-free ring or pre-allocated iovec combos for the common path.

maria: timeline: I'm rolling kv flag revert to canary now. Will post metrics in 5m.

(infra-bot): canary rollout started: service=hosting-gw config=kv.prefix_invalidate=false target=10%

aj: while that's rolling, I'll push a small gate-change to coalesce writes on the gw. Patch is minimal: `if accumulated_len >= 32768 || now - last_flush >= 3ms -> flush`

ken: pushed kernel-policy patch to my branch. Need perf harness to validate before merging.

maria: canary metrics: tail latency down ~6% already, KV evictions down ~30%, but writev count still high (down ~10%).

sophia: nice. that's promising.

aj: coalesce PR landed to canary. If we see no regressions I'll expand. Also added a test in gateway integration: sim streaming many frames and assert single syscall count < 4 per response.

maria: observed one surprising thing: tokenization CPU per-request dropped but overall p50 didn't move much; it's p95 that moves. suspect backpressure from parsing queue.

ken: try bumping parse worker pool from 8 -> 12 for a quick canary. If parse queue latency is causing scheduling waits that's cheap to test.

maria: bumped parse workers on canary -> p95 improved another ~3%. Combined with coalesce + kv revert we're back within baseline.

aj: follow-ups:
- runtime: add kernel selection unit tests and expose a metric `kernel_variant_chosen{seq_bucket}`
- gateway: keep coalescing and add adaptive coalesce (based on client frame size distribution)
- kv: audit invalidation code paths and add histograms for eviction reasons
- obs: automated microprofile capture for deploys that change network/pathing

sophia: I'll open a small playbook in docs for reproducer + test harness.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll keep thread updated when we roll the full rollout. :thumbsup:

aj: nice triage. quick note: if anyone runs local reproducer use `--nolocalcache` flag to avoid noisy host cache differences.

ken: adding perf artifacts to the PRs.

(infra-bot): canary rollout: kv.prefix_invalidate=false -> 50%

maria: full rollout completed at 04:20, metrics stable, closing incident. Thanks! :tada:
